articles.originalTitle: US taxpayer group calls on ICC to investigate Trump, Rubio for 'aiding' Gaza genocide
articles.originalDescription: US taxpayer group calls on ICC to investigate Trump, Rubio for 'aiding' Gaza genocide Submitted by MEE staff on Wed, 11/11/2026 - 18:54 The complainants say they have exhausted all other legal options to seek justice Seth Donnelly, co-founder of the Taxpayers Alliance Against Genocide, leads a press conference from The Hague, in the Netherlands, to announce an official submission to the ICC to investigate US President Donald Trump and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, on 11 November 2026 (Screengrab) Off A group of US taxpayers and international human rights lawyers have officially called on the International Criminal Court (ICC) to investigate President Donald Trump and his top diplomat Marco Rubio for "aiding and abetting genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity committed by Israel in Gaza". They announced it at a press conference at the court's home in The Hague, in the Netherlands, on Wednesday. The submission to the court was organised by the Taxpayer Alliance Against Genocide (Taag), and includes sworn affidavits from doctors who worked in Gaza, firsthand eyewitness accounts, whistleblower testimony, video evidence, and extensive documentation of what they say is US military, financial, diplomatic, and political support for Israel, the group said. Among those involved are Dr Feroze Sidhwa , a trauma surgeon who undertook two missions in Gaza, and David McIntosh , a former contractor with the scandal-plagued and now-defunct Gaza Humanitarian Foundation, both of whom have previously shared their detailed experiences with Middle East Eye. It took nearly a year to compile the necessary proof that without the US, Israel could not have carried out what the United Nations and Holocaust scholars have described as a genocide of Palestinians in Gaza, Taag said in a press release accompanying the announcement. articles.originalDescription: UN humanitarian chief says 'no more excuses' on opening Gaza crossing UN under-secretary-general for humanitarian affairs and emergency relief coordinator Tom Fletcher said on Wednesday that there cannot be any more delays in opening the border crossings into Gaza to deliver humanitarian aid. "No more delays. No more excuses. We must open all the crossings, mobilize the whole humanitarian community, and get our full Winter plan delivered for Gaza," Fletcher wrote in a post on X. articles.title: Sidang ulang jurnalis Mesir Lina Attalah ditunda di tengah kritik media yang rusak
articles.description: Persidangan ulang jurnalis Mesir Lina Attalah ditunda di tengah kritikan media yang patah hati diturunkan oleh staf MEE pada Wed, 11 / 11 / 2026 - 10: 13 Mada Pengacara editor Masr mengatakan hakim telah membentuk pandangan terhadap dirinya setelah memesan outlet 's penutupan terpisah dalam kasus Mada Masr pendiri dan editor- di - kepala Lina Attalah berbicara selama wawancara di Kairo pada 8 November 2026 (Khaled Desouki / AFP) Pengadilan Mesir pada hari Rabu menunda sidang ulang dari Mada Masr -in -kepala Lina Attalah sampai 18 November untuk mempertimbangkan permintaan pertahanan untuk membuang berita independen. Attalah menghadapi tuntutan penerbitan berita palsu dan mengoperasikan sebuah situs tanpa izin dalam sebuah kasus di mana dia dijatuhi hukuman setahun penjara karena ketidakhadirannya pada tahun 2024. Pengacara Mada Masr, Hassan Al- Azhari, mengatakan pertahanan akan mengajukan alasan untuk mencari hakim penghapusan depan sidang berikutnya, berpendapat bahwa ia telah "sudah membentuk pandangan terhadap terdakwa". Hakim ketua, Mohamed Mubarak, juga mengeluarkan putusan pada 27 Oktober dalam kasus terpisah fining Attalah tiga juta pound Mesir (sekitar $56.000) dan memerintahkan penutupan Mada Masr' s. Proses ini terjadi di tengah banyaknya media independen yang lebih luas, termasuk penahanan pada bulan September dari enam jurnalis yang bekerja untuk pemeriksaan wajah-outlet Matsadash. Mada Masr mengatakan Attalah menerima panggilan dalam kasus lisensi terbaru pada 19 Oktober, jam setelah bergabung dengan tujuh lainnya independen media Arab dalam berita independen inisiatif dimaksudkan untuk mengisi kesenjangan kiri oleh penangkapan Matsadaash. Dana HSBC mulai pelacakan S & P Global 1200 Shariah Pilih Indeks, sebuah tanda tangan perusahaan disaring untuk kepatuhan dengan prinsip keuangan Islam, pada Maret. Dana tersebut secara pasif dikelola, yang berarti itu mencerminkan investasi indeks. articles.originalDescription: US House Democrat leader Jeffries will retain position despite opposition, sources say Submitted by Yasmine El-Sabawi on Tue, 11/10/2026 - 19:15 In the Senate, unless progressive-backed Chris Van Hollen formally steps up to unite the ranks as a challenger, Chuck Schumer will likely win The leader of the House Democrats, New York Congressman Hakeem Jeffries, right, speaks to reporters alongside the leader of the Senate Democrats, New York Senator Chuck Schumer, on the steps of the US Senate on 21 May 2026 in Washington, DC (Win McNamee/Getty Images via AFP) Off The top Democrat in the House of Representatives, Hakeem Jeffries, is all but certain to become the next Speaker of the House, despite dissatisfaction among some freshman lawmakers and their progressive colleagues in the chamber, sources have told Middle East Eye. There simply is no alternative leader in the running. "It's a cost to go against someone who will eventually be the leader of the caucus. There's not enough people who are willing to do that," one source said. This comes as many voters have expressed their desire to see Jeffries vacate the position, accusing him of being out of step with the party's growing leftist progressive wing, which wants to see money out of politics, and a stop to the transfer of weapons to Israel. articles.originalTitle: Gaza sandbank collapse kills five amid heavy rains
articles.originalDescription: Gaza sandbank collapse kills five amid heavy rains At least five people have been killed, including three children, after heavy rains caused a sandbank to collapse in central Gaza's Deir al-Balah, Wafa news reported on Sunday. A civil defence spokesman added that five wounded people had been pulled out of the rubble after their tents were hit, and teams are continuing to search for survivors. The incident comes amid worsening conditions faced by displaced Palestinians in Gaza, as national and internation institutions warned heavy rainfall and bad weather require urgent intervention and the provision of safe shelter and winter supplies.
